note: Spambot checks user-registration (and Webform) email/username/IP against the Stop Forum Spam (www.stopforumspam.com) blacklist. All configuration lives in the single config object spambot.settings (form route spambot.settings_form at /admin/config/system/spambot). Thresholds spambot_criteria_email (default 1), spambot_criteria_username (default 0/off), spambot_criteria_ip (default 20); a criterion of 0 disables that check. Whitelists are spambot_whitelist_{email,username,ip}_list arrays. Cron scanning is gated by spambot_cron_user_limit with spambot_spam_account_action (0 none/1 block/2 delete). The permission 'protected from spambot scans' bypasses all checks. Reporting spammers needs spambot_sfs_api_key. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real spambot.settings keys, read/written via drush cget/cset.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal spambot module, which external blacklist service does it check new registrations against, and which configuration keys set the per-criterion thresholds for email and IP address?
evals.expected_output: It queries Stop Forum Spam (www.stopforumspam.com). Thresholds are spambot_criteria_email and spambot_criteria_ip (and spambot_criteria_username) in spambot.settings; a value of 0 disables that check.

evals.prompt: Which Drupal permission does the spambot module provide, and what does granting it to a role do?
evals.expected_output: The single permission is 'protected from spambot scans'. A user/role holding it bypasses all spambot checks: the registration validator is not attached and cron scans take no block/delete action against those accounts.

evals.prompt: There is no obvious settings link for spambot. What is the name of the configuration object that stores all spambot settings, and what is the admin form route/path?
evals.expected_output: All settings live in the spambot.settings config object; the admin form is route spambot.settings_form at /admin/config/system/spambot (requires 'administer site configuration').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, spambot is configured with a specific threshold for how many times an IP address must have been reported to Stop Forum Spam before a registration is blocked. Inspect the live configuration and state that IP-address threshold number.
evals.expected_output: spambot.settings:spambot_criteria_ip is 13 on this site (drush cget spambot.settings spambot_criteria_ip).

evals.prompt: This site has one email address on spambot's email whitelist (so it is exempt from spam checks). Inspect the live spambot configuration and give that whitelisted email address.
On this Drupal site, configure spambot so that a user registration is blocked when the chosen username has been reported to Stop Forum Spam at least 5 times. Apply the change to the live site.
Add the IP address 198.51.100.7 to spambot's IP whitelist on this site so that spambot never checks or blocks that address. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Add 198.51.100.7 to the spambot.settings:spambot_whitelist_ip_list array and save (e.g. drush cset spambot.settings spambot_whitelist_ip_list.0 198.51.100.7 -y, or set the full array in php:eval).
